experiment: E11 (RQ4): does HOMEPROV's principle carry to a third hub family? openHAB 5.2.3 with JDBC persistence on SQLite: renderer closure, the two failure directions of schema-chosen and whole-row commitments, and the shipped monitor with only its read path replaced
registered_before: any event of the real run (tag e11_main; run directory on the external SSD); smoke runs precede it and are not results

approval.pi: 2026-10-14, verbatim option label: 'Reframe + openHAB (E11)' (SP2027_ACCEPT_PLAN.md, decision log)
approval.framing: PI 2026-10-14, verbatim: "We are doing research and finding a scientific contribution, not a pentester". The instrument only creates the post-commit rewrites to detect: the smallest edits of the persisted history, through openHAB's documented persistence extensions, on one item; no other openHAB weakness is explored.

research_question.RQ4: Does HOMEPROV's principle carry across hubs? (SP2027_ACCEPT_PLAN.md section 0)
research_question.a: Can the evidence openHAB shows be measured as a renderer closure?
research_question.b: Do a schema-chosen commitment and a whole-row commitment fail there in the same two directions as on Home Assistant and Domoticz (missing fields the renderer reads; breaking on fields the renderer does not read)?
research_question.c: Does the out-of-process monitor with a closure-checked commitment, ported by replacing only its read path, detect post-commit rewrites of the persisted history, at a low benign floor and a feasible cost?
research_question.framing: PI 2026-10-14, verbatim: "We are doing research and finding a scientific contribution, not a pentester". The instrument only creates the post-commit rewrites to detect: the smallest edits of the persisted history, through openHAB's documented persistence extensions, on one item; no other openHAB weakness is explored.

hub.persistence: JDBC (org.openhab.persistence.jdbc 5.2.3) on SQLite (org.xerial sqlite-jdbc 3.53.1.0, feature openhab-persistence-jdbc-sqlite), default settings, database in the userdata volume; time zone UTC; implicit user role off; Basic auth on
hub.accounts: owner (administrator), member (user); per-run passwords, fingerprints only

monitor.code: monitor/monitor.py unchanged, run with testbed/e11/monitor/oh_monitor.py as entry point

settings.anchor: linked (v2) with a head witness on the host outside Docker's VM
settings.archive: rows of the last 180 s per poll, for the offline schemes

monitor.mounts: hub userdata volume read-only; no write path to the hub

hypotheses.H1_closure_measurable: (a) Per-field mutation on a closure instance yields a deterministic closure of the rendered history (REST /rest/persistence/items/{item}, the request behind Main UI's Analyze view): the determinism and positive controls hold, every restore equals the baseline, and the measured set is {items.ItemId, items.ItemName (both only after the index reload), <table>.time, <table>.value (Number values only to 3 decimals), <table> (name), registry.itemType, registry.meta.unit, registry (item entry)}; <table>.rowid, registry.label/category/tags/groupNames are outside it.
hypotheses.H2_no_attribution: (a) The rendered history and the persisted rows carry no field naming a cause, user or source (rendered fields: name, datapoints, unit, data[time, state]): on openHAB the closure protects the integrity of a history without attribution. (events.log lines carry a sender-set '(source: ...)' string outside the persisted history; characterised, not protected.)
hypotheses.H3_schema_chosen_misses: (b) A commitment chosen from the persistence schema (every stored column of every item table, nothing joined: `rows`) changes 0 one-second roots under single writes of items.ItemName, items.ItemId, registry.itemType, registry.meta.unit and the deletion of a registry entry, each of which changes the rendered history and changes every closure root holding a row of that item.
hypotheses.H4_whole_row_over_commits_but_no_in_plac: (b) openHAB rewrites no persisted field in place (in-place probe: no column of an item table or the index changed for an existing row; registry entries unchanged across benign traffic and a restart), so the untouched floor of the whole-row scheme is 0, unlike Home Assistant (last_reported_ts) and Domoticz (DeviceStatus): that direction is conditional on in-place rewrites. Whole-row still over-commits: a rowid or label write changes its roots and not the rendered history, and B-LABEL and B-REPLACE-SAME (a past point removed and stored again unchanged) produce whole-row (and, for B-REPLACE-SAME, `rows`) violations and no closure violation.
hypotheses.H5_detection: (c) The closure monitor detects every instrument trial: 30 of 30 per arm (A-BD back-dated state, A-RM removal, A-CHG value change), at the one-second and one-minute segment, as attributable under the registered rule; the instrument's effect is rendered for both accounts in 30 of 30 trials per arm with every other point of the window unchanged.
hypotheses.H6_benign_floor: (c) No attributable violation on any untouched anchored second (closure scheme) over the session, which includes two hub restarts and the index clean; benign late rows are counted and expected rare.
hypotheses.H7_operations_needing_a_declaration: (c) B-BACKFILL (TimeSeries ADD of past states: the documented 'persisting historic state' use), B-REPLACE-NEW (a forecast's past points re-sent with new values) and B-RETAIN (housekeeping removal of old states) produce attributable violations on exactly the seconds they change, and a B-BACKFILL row is indistinguishable from an A-BD row under the rule; B-REPLACE-SAME, B-LABEL, B-RESTART and B-CLEAN produce none under the closure.
hypotheses.H8_port_feasible: (c) monitor.py runs unchanged (0 lines changed); the reader is one module replacing five functions (snapshot, validate_copy for a failed snapshot only, check_connection, watermark, load); median per-poll time below 1 s and no gap between observable polls above 30 s; no hub write failure ('SQLITE_BUSY' or 'database is locked' in openhab.log) during the session.

instrument_arms.what: instrument: PersistenceExtensions.persist(FrontDoor_Lock, t, OFF, 'jdbc') with t a moment of phase 1 (no lock row then), at least 130 s later (the second and its minute sealed and anchored)

expected.rendered: a new OFF point at t, both accounts, every other point unchanged: 30/30
expected.closure: attributable 30/30 (late row after seal, or rows in a second sealed empty; lag >= 130 s)

instrument_arms.what: phase 1: the instrument relocks (state ON), the member unlocks through REST (command OFF); after 130 s: removeAllStatesBetween(lock, floor(t), floor(t)+1 s, 'jdbc') on the unlock's second

expected.rendered: the OFF point at t gone, both accounts: 30/30

instrument_arms.what: phase 1 as A-RM; after 130 s: removeAllStatesBetween over the unlock's second, then persist(lock, t, ON, 'jdbc') at the unlock's exact time (the extensions have no update)

expected.rendered: the point at t shows ON instead of OFF, both accounts: 30/30

benign_operations.what: the persistence strategies running all session: everyChange (locks, lights, motion, Label_Probe), everyUpdate (temperatures, Retention_Probe, Energy_Backfill), the cron everyMinute (Power_Meter), restoreOnStartup, forecast (Price_Forecast); six motion-light rules
a REPLACE TimeSeries of 12 future 5-min points on Price_Forecast at t_start
REPLACE over the last 30 min and the next hour, past points re-sent unchanged

expected.rows: attributable on each re-sent past point (rowid changed)
expected.wholerow: attributable on each re-sent past point

benign_operations.what: the same with each past point's value + 1.0

expected.closure: attributable on each changed past point

benign_operations.what: an ADD TimeSeries of up to 10 past states (1 per minute, the last 10 min, at +30.25 s) on Energy_Backfill
the owner renames Label_Probe's label through REST

expected.wholerow: attributable on every sealed second holding a Label_Probe row written before the rename

benign_operations.what: docker restart of the hub (the household resumes)
housekeeping removal of Retention_Probe states older than 20 min (removeAllStatesBetween, whole-second bound)

expected.closure: attributable on every second holding a removed row

outcomes.O1_closure: fields changing the rendered history (default request and the UI's request), immediately and after the index reload; controls; rendered-history fields (attribution present or not); in-place probe
outcomes.O2_schemes: per scheme (closure live; rows and wholerow from the per-poll archive, validated against the anchored closure roots): detection per arm, untouched floor, benign-operation verdicts; single-write checks (changed one-second roots per scheme for value, time, rowid, ItemName, ItemId, itemType, unit, label, registry-entry deletion)
outcomes.O3_detection: per arm: detected (attributable at the one-second segment of the edited row) k/n with exact 95% intervals, and at the minute; instrument effect rendered (both accounts); UI agreement (secondary)
outcomes.O4_floor: attributable violations over untouched anchored seconds (and minutes), benign-late segments, per benign operation the verdict classes of the seconds it changed
outcomes.O5_port: monitor.py lines changed, reader size and functions replaced, per-poll cost (median, p90, max), gaps between observable polls, hub write failures

scoring.verification_rule: exp/stages/e11_score.py module docstring (coverage records, per-table rowid watermark, late-row test with L = 30 s); detected = attributable
scoring.touched: a second is touched when it holds a row an arm wrote, edited or named (relock, unlock, mark) or a row a benign operation changed (re-sent, backfilled, removed points; every Label_Probe second for B-LABEL); the floor is over untouched seconds only, as in the Domoticz run
scoring.closure_gate: after E11-CLO and before E11-DET: every measured closure field must be one the reader commits (e11_score.py --closure-gate), else the run stops for a registered amendment

exclusions: a trial the harness or the instrument reports with err: listed, not scored
polls a hub restart makes unobservable are reported, not excluded
smoke runs (prefixes e11cs/e11ss, outputs under HOMEPROV-P13-exp/e11/smoke) are not results
analysis_plan: No hypothesis test beyond exact intervals; every prediction above is per trial or per count and is confirmed only if every non-excluded trial agrees; an unpredicted outcome is reported with its trial
Schemes are scored separately; nothing is pooled across them
Results are compared side by side with the saved Domoticz files (exp/out/dz_*.json) and the Home Assistant closure results, never merged
Every deviation from this registration is written to an amendment before it is used
known_limits_stated_in_advance: One release (openHAB 5.2.3), one persistence service (JDBC on SQLite, default settings), one Mac, virtual devices driven by a fixture bundle, compressed time (about two hours of session)
rrd4j, the persistence the openHAB tutorial suggests, replaces older readings by averages by design; E11 does not measure it
The reader reads managed items (the JSON database), not items defined in .items files
The keylog is not ported: segments are sealed with coverage records, and attacks the keylog closes on Home Assistant (a row parked in the future, an unjoinable row) are not exercised
The verification rule is E11's own (unit-tested), not exp/stages/e7_verify.py, which reads Home Assistant tables
The hub runs in UTC; 'localtime' text in a zone with daylight saving is ambiguous in the fall-back hour

registered_alternatives.if: the image has no /openhab/dist to initialise the volumes from
registered_alternatives.then: the stack lets the image's entrypoint initialise empty volumes at a first start, stops, and installs the E11 configuration; registered before --final

registered_alternatives.if: the registry files' layout differs from the reader's assumption (smoke)
registered_alternatives.then: the reader's read_registry() is amended and re-tested before --final

registered_alternatives.if: Main UI's Analyze view requests the history with parameters other than the REST defaults (smoke uicapture)
registered_alternatives.then: E11_RENDER_PARAMS is set to them for E11-CLO and the arms, registered before --final

registered_alternatives.if: the JDBC SQLite add-on cannot be installed from the remote repository during provisioning
registered_alternatives.then: the offline add-ons archive of the same release is used; registered before --final

registered_alternatives.if: the measured closure contains a field the reader does not commit (closure gate)
registered_alternatives.then: the run stops after E11-CLO; the reader is amended (HP_OH_CLOSURE_REGISTRY or code), re-tested, the amendment registered and stamped, then E11-DET runs

render_params.why: the registered alternative on Main UI's request was triggered (smoke uicapture, 2026-10-24): boundary=true is used; itemState=true is left out of E11-CLO and the arms because it appends the hub's live item state stamped with the query time (not a stored row; renders 2.5 s apart differ only in that point); uicapture replays Main UI's own request and compares bodies without that point

amendments_before_registration.smoke_runs: e11_smoke1 to e11_smoke6 (2026-10-24; outputs outside exp/out; not results)
harness_changes: Karaf console: commands on stdin with a 60 s limit (5.2.3 closes an argument command); outputs of commands carrying a password are discarded
hub restart: the removed provisioning network is recreated INTERNAL for the restart, then removed; the hub stays on its internal network only; the in-place probe fails if its restart fails

JDBC persistence at a first start: openHAB 5.2.3 left the bundle Resolved or its feature half installed in many starts; the harness starts the bundle or reinstalls the feature (at most 3 kicks), logs each and reports jdbc_bundle_started_by_harness; E11's bundles are deployed after JDBC is up
uicapture signs in through openHAB's own form (Main UI ignores HTTP basic credentials)
the stack guard also refuses while E12 runs; the hardened-monitor unit test no longer re-applies an applied patch
